Almost certainly not with normal unaided eyesight.

Although the Moon is geometrically **16.8° above the horizon**, it is only **1.32% illuminated** and just **13.17° from the Sun**. With the Sun still **5.1° above the horizon**, the sky near the Moon would remain very bright. The Moon is also low in the western sky, where atmospheric extinction and haze further reduce the crescent’s contrast.

This would be an exceptionally difficult daylight crescent observation, likely requiring optical aid and very clear, transparent conditions. So while the Moon is technically above the horizon, for practical naked-eye purposes you can reasonably expect it to be **invisible** at that moment.

Do not scan near the Sun with binoculars or a telescope unless the Sun is securely blocked and appropriate solar-safety procedures are used.
